title: Ropedia Xperience-10M Glossary
purpose: Define reader-facing project terms and adjacent technical field terms for embodied AI, egocentric multimodal data, spatial intelligence, world models, VLA/policy learning, evaluation, and public artifact reading.

categories.label: Dataset and scope
categories.description: Public data boundaries, evidence lines, and how each result family should be read.

categories.label: Files and features
categories.description: Raw sample files, windows, feature manifests, and public-safe derivatives.

categories.label: Multimodal sensing
categories.description: Video, audio, depth, IMU, motion capture, calibration, and synchronization terms.

categories.label: Spatial geometry
categories.description: Camera pose, SLAM, coordinate frames, point clouds, 3D reconstruction, and spatial grounding.

categories.label: Temporal and world models
categories.description: Future prediction, rollouts, forward dynamics, long-horizon forecasting, and temporal leakage.

categories.label: Robotics and VLA
categories.description: Vision-language-action, policies, action chunks, imitation learning, contact, and dexterity.

categories.label: Tasks and metrics
categories.description: Task contracts, scored records, direct scores, compact proxies, and audits.

categories.label: Training and evaluation
categories.description: Splits, held-out evaluation, metric types, prompt/schema checks, adapters, and distributed training.

categories.label: Models and runs
categories.description: Baseline families, Qwen3-Omni, Cosmos3, LoRA adapters, and full-parameter gates.

categories.label: Public surfaces
categories.description: GitHub, website, Hugging Face repos, parity checks, and package validation.

entries.plain_meaning: A reading lane for a group of results.
entries.project_usage: Line 1 is one public sample episode; Line 2 is selected-128 held-out comparison.
entries.do_not_confuse_with: Qwen run versions v1-v6, which are model-run lineage.

entries.plain_meaning: Upstream files that require official dataset access.
entries.project_usage: Raw Xperience-10M MP4/HDF5/RRD files and full source directories remain outside the public repo.
entries.do_not_confuse_with: Public-safe metrics, derived features, figures, and manifests.

entries.plain_meaning: One officially available sample episode.
entries.project_usage: The fully inspectable Line 1 unit used for raw-file browsing, 20-frame windows, task construction, and single-episode baselines.

entries.plain_meaning: A public-safe selected subset of official gated episode paths.
entries.project_usage: Line 2 uses derived windows/features and keeps links back to official episode ids and gated source paths.

entries.plain_meaning: The upstream embodied human-interaction dataset.
entries.project_usage: Source dataset behind the public sample, selected-128 features, task suite, and model diagnostics.
entries.do_not_confuse_with: This repo, which only redistributes public-safe derived artifacts.

entries.plain_meaning: A fixed short clip slice.
entries.project_usage: The sample episode is converted into aligned 20-frame units for features, labels, and many task heads.
entries.do_not_confuse_with: A full episode or arbitrary video segment.

entries.plain_meaning: Upstream annotation container for the sample.
entries.project_usage: Contains original labels/metadata; some public derived files expose processed features instead of every raw text field.

entries.plain_meaning: One recorded interaction sequence.
entries.project_usage: The basic source unit behind windows, labels, and train/val/test splits.

entries.plain_meaning: A map from model-input columns to source modalities.
entries.project_usage: Explains feature groups and dimensions for the sample task suite.

entries.plain_meaning: Natural-language interaction/caption content.
entries.project_usage: Used by task 15 and some derived text features; public matrices record direct or compact-proxy status.
entries.do_not_confuse_with: Numeric action ids or subtask ids.

entries.plain_meaning: A type of signal.
entries.project_usage: Video, audio, depth, pose/SLAM, motion capture, inertial, calibration, and language-derived signals.

entries.plain_meaning: A human-readable inventory of the sample episode files.
entries.project_usage: Explains videos, annotations, calibration, motion, and derived previews.

entries.plain_meaning: Rerun viewer recording for visual inspection.
entries.project_usage: Can be downloaded from the official sample dataset and opened in Rerun 0.29.0 to inspect the sample episode. It is not used for published training or metric rows.
entries.do_not_confuse_with: MP4 video streams or model inputs.

entries.plain_meaning: The frame step between neighboring windows.
entries.project_usage: Creates overlapping examples while preserving chronological order and leakage controls.

entries.plain_meaning: A time-series pressure signal from sound.
entries.project_usage: The audio ablation measures whether embedded audio helps selected task contracts.

entries.plain_meaning: Parameters that relate sensors to each other and to physical space.
entries.project_usage: Needed to interpret camera streams, depth, pose, and synchronized multimodal features together.

entries.plain_meaning: A camera position and orientation relative to another coordinate frame.
entries.project_usage: Connects different camera streams and world coordinates.

entries.plain_meaning: Internal camera parameters such as focal length and distortion.
entries.project_usage: Explain how image pixels project to rays for geometry tasks.

entries.plain_meaning: A per-pixel estimate of distance from the camera.
entries.project_usage: Depth-derived signals support spatial and geometry-oriented tasks.

entries.plain_meaning: Video captured from a first-person or body-mounted viewpoint.
entries.project_usage: The sample streams are egocentric views of human interaction and are the visual basis for many tasks.

entries.plain_meaning: A wide-angle camera with strong lens distortion.
entries.project_usage: Multiple fisheye MP4 streams give broad room coverage but need calibration-aware interpretation.

entries.plain_meaning: An inertial measurement unit with accelerometer and gyroscope signals.
entries.project_usage: Supports motion, temporal, and sensor-bridging tasks.

entries.plain_meaning: Depth expressed in physical units rather than arbitrary relative scale.
entries.project_usage: Useful for distance-sensitive spatial reasoning and reconstruction targets.

entries.plain_meaning: A system that records body or hand motion over time.
entries.project_usage: Provides hand/body motion evidence when exposed through public-safe derived features.

entries.plain_meaning: A color image frame from a video stream.
entries.project_usage: Used for visual statistics, previews, and many model inputs.

entries.plain_meaning: Putting different sensor streams into a shared temporal or spatial reference.
entries.project_usage: Used to make video, audio, pose, depth, IMU, and mocap usable in the same task input.

entries.plain_meaning: A paired-camera setup that supports depth or geometry estimation.
entries.project_usage: The sample browser exposes stereo streams as part of the visual modality set.

entries.plain_meaning: Aligning sensor samples by time.
entries.project_usage: The task suite assumes aligned windows across modalities so labels and features refer to the same moment.
entries.do_not_confuse_with: Randomly joining files with similar names.

entries.plain_meaning: Recovering 3D scene structure from sensor data.
entries.project_usage: One core spatial-intelligence direction for Xperience-style data.

entries.plain_meaning: An action possibility offered by an object or scene.
entries.project_usage: Relevant when moving from observed human interaction to robot-action or VLA tasks.

entries.plain_meaning: The camera position and orientation at a time step.
entries.project_usage: Supports spatial-intelligence tasks, view synchronization, and geometry diagnostics.

entries.plain_meaning: A reference system for positions and orientations.
entries.project_usage: Needed when comparing camera, body, object, and world measurements.

entries.plain_meaning: A representation organized around objects and their relations.
entries.project_usage: Useful for object relevance, object-set forecast, and action-object relation tasks.
entries.do_not_confuse_with: A flat feature vector without object identity.

entries.plain_meaning: Motion estimated from sensor changes over time.
entries.project_usage: A relevant spatial term for ego-motion and camera-pose reasoning.

entries.plain_meaning: A set of 3D points representing scene structure.
entries.project_usage: A likely target or intermediate representation for spatial-intelligence extensions.

entries.plain_meaning: Simultaneous localization and mapping.
entries.project_usage: A field term for estimating camera motion and scene structure from sensor observations.
entries.do_not_confuse_with: A task label or action class.

entries.plain_meaning: Linking language or labels to locations, objects, or geometry.
entries.project_usage: Connects language grounding tasks with 3D/spatial reasoning.

entries.plain_meaning: A sequence of positions over time.
entries.project_usage: Used for hand motion, camera motion, and future-path tasks.

entries.plain_meaning: Predicting a future action before it happens.
entries.project_usage: Covered by next-action and long-horizon task contracts.

entries.plain_meaning: Generating each future token, state, or frame conditioned on prior outputs.
entries.project_usage: Relevant for model branches that produce structured JSON or temporal predictions.

entries.plain_meaning: Predicting the next state from the current state and action/context.
entries.project_usage: The Cosmos3-Super LoRA branch uses a forward-dynamics-style diagnostic contract.
entries.do_not_confuse_with: Reverse inference from result back to cause.

entries.plain_meaning: A hidden representation that summarizes observed context.
entries.project_usage: Useful for future foundation-model and world-model training plans.

entries.plain_meaning: Predicting outcomes several seconds or steps ahead.
entries.project_usage: Tasks 13 and 14 test longer temporal context beyond immediate recognition.

entries.plain_meaning: Predicting future visual frames from past frames.
entries.project_usage: A field-level world-model objective related to the human-video world-model direction.

entries.plain_meaning: Tracking that an object remains present over time even when view or interaction changes.
entries.project_usage: Relevant for object-set forecast and long-video reasoning.

entries.plain_meaning: Repeatedly predicting future steps from a model state.
entries.project_usage: Important for judging world models beyond one-step prediction.

entries.plain_meaning: Predicting the next higher-level step in an activity.
entries.project_usage: Used in the future-task probe line for Qwen3-Omni.

entries.plain_meaning: Training a sequence model using ground-truth previous outputs.
entries.project_usage: A likely training option for future sequence/world-model baselines.

entries.plain_meaning: Using future information that would not be available at prediction time.
entries.project_usage: Avoided by chronological splits and target-side feature controls.

entries.plain_meaning: Estimating when the next state or action transition happens.
entries.project_usage: Task 20 turns temporal change into a regression target.

entries.plain_meaning: A short sequence of low-level actions predicted together.
entries.project_usage: The VLA figure and plan use action chunks as the policy-output concept.

entries.plain_meaning: A supervised imitation-learning method for predicting demonstrated actions.
entries.project_usage: A plausible baseline once action targets are converted.

entries.plain_meaning: A moment when a hand, body, or tool touches an object or surface.
entries.project_usage: Used in contact-related tasks and action-quality interpretation.

entries.plain_meaning: Fine-grained physical manipulation ability.
entries.project_usage: Relevant to hand-object interaction, contact, and VLA/policy directions.

entries.plain_meaning: The robot part that acts on the world, such as a gripper or hand.
entries.project_usage: A key target frame for future manipulation-policy conversion.
entries.do_not_confuse_with: A camera or global scene coordinate.

entries.plain_meaning: A physical interaction between hands and objects.
entries.project_usage: A central signal family behind action, contact, object relevance, and interaction-text tasks.

entries.plain_meaning: Training a policy to imitate demonstrated behavior.
entries.project_usage: Relevant when converting human video/motion into action supervision.
entries.do_not_confuse_with: Reinforcement learning from online robot trials.

entries.plain_meaning: Connecting text to observed objects, actions, or spatial context.
entries.project_usage: Task 8 and VLA directions use language as grounded supervision rather than standalone text.

entries.plain_meaning: A mapping from observations to actions.
entries.project_usage: A future target for robot-compatible Xperience-derived action data.

entries.plain_meaning: An action representation a robot policy can execute or imitate.
entries.project_usage: Needed before OpenVLA/openpi/GR00T-style policy training is meaningful here.

entries.plain_meaning: A model that maps visual context and language into actions.
entries.project_usage: The VLA direction is a future path after action targets are converted into robot-compatible chunks.
entries.do_not_confuse_with: A vision-language model that only answers text.

entries.plain_meaning: A bounded proxy metric when a direct raw target is not publicly available.
entries.project_usage: Kept explicit in the matrix and gap audit so readers do not over-read it.

entries.plain_meaning: A metric computed against the task target directly.
entries.project_usage: The preferred score type in the 20-task matrix.

entries.plain_meaning: A coverage and source-status audit.
entries.project_usage: Explains scored, proxy, and unsupported cells.

entries.plain_meaning: A split or feature rule that prevents using target information unfairly.
entries.project_usage: Chronological splits, held-out splits, and source audits protect task interpretation.

entries.plain_meaning: A 0-1 plotting value used only to draw comparable radar polygons.
entries.project_usage: Helps visualize metrics with different scales and directions.
entries.do_not_confuse_with: The raw metric value to cite.

entries.plain_meaning: The original metric value emitted by the runner or verified result package.
entries.project_usage: This is the value to cite from the 180-result table.

entries.plain_meaning: The definition of one benchmark task.
entries.project_usage: Includes input, target/output, metric, split, source artifact, and limitation.

entries.plain_meaning: One method evaluated on one task.
entries.project_usage: 9 methods x 20 tasks gives 180 public result records.

entries.plain_meaning: The current task surface.
entries.project_usage: All 20 task contracts are presented together and scored across methods where real artifacts exist.
entries.do_not_confuse_with: Historical tier2_task_suite filenames, which are provenance paths rather than a second suite.

entries.plain_meaning: Saved adapter weights from a fine-tuning run.
entries.project_usage: The public model branches publish adapters when validated and public-safe.

entries.plain_meaning: Accuracy averaged across classes to reduce majority-class dominance.
entries.project_usage: Useful for imbalanced task labels.

entries.plain_meaning: A split ordered by time.
entries.project_usage: Used for the single-episode baselines to reduce future-window leakage.

entries.plain_meaning: A table of predicted classes versus true classes.
entries.project_usage: Helps inspect which task labels a method confuses.

entries.plain_meaning: Fully Sharded Data Parallel, a distributed training strategy.
entries.project_usage: Appears in full-parameter feasibility and multi-GPU training notes.

entries.plain_meaning: Testing on examples not used for training.
entries.project_usage: Required before promoting Qwen/Cosmos results to public evidence.

entries.plain_meaning: Whether model output parses as the required JSON schema.
entries.project_usage: A key diagnostic for Qwen3-Omni structured-output runs.

entries.plain_meaning: The average F1 score across classes, usually treating classes equally.
entries.project_usage: Used when class imbalance matters in classification tasks.

entries.plain_meaning: The average absolute difference between predicted and true numeric values.
entries.project_usage: Used for regression-style task rows such as timing or trajectory targets.

entries.plain_meaning: A small training test that verifies a model can learn a tiny subset.
entries.project_usage: Useful for catching data/model wiring bugs before full training.

entries.plain_meaning: Updating a small number of added or selected parameters.
entries.project_usage: LoRA is the current parameter-efficient path for Qwen/Cosmos branches.

entries.plain_meaning: Whether an output follows the expected field names and value types.
entries.project_usage: Needed for structured task probes and public package validation.

entries.plain_meaning: A short run that checks whether a pipeline can start and execute key steps.
entries.project_usage: Used for feasibility gates before expensive full runs.

entries.plain_meaning: A score that counts a prediction correct if the target is among the k highest-ranked outputs.
entries.project_usage: Useful for large-label or retrieval-style tasks.

entries.plain_meaning: A partition that separates model fitting, tuning, and final evaluation examples.
entries.project_usage: The selected-128 setup uses a held-out split discipline for model branches.
entries.do_not_confuse_with: A random shuffle without temporal or episode boundaries.

entries.plain_meaning: A smaller Cosmos3 compatibility/future-window branch.
entries.project_usage: Used for the Nano Future Window row and related diagnostics.

entries.plain_meaning: The larger Cosmos3-style branch tracked in this project.
entries.project_usage: Published as Reasoner diagnostics and a separate forward-dynamics LoRA adapter/result branch when verified.

entries.plain_meaning: A high-level training direction.
entries.project_usage: Spatial intelligence, human-video world modeling, and vision-language-action are documented as trainable directions with task mappings.

entries.plain_meaning: Updating the whole model rather than only adapters.
entries.project_usage: This project records feasibility gates and short pilots, but does not publish full checkpoints.

entries.plain_meaning: Learning future frames, actions, and interaction dynamics from human video.
entries.project_usage: Uses temporal prediction, next-action, transition, and object-forecast tasks.

entries.plain_meaning: A lightweight set of trainable adapter weights.
entries.project_usage: Published only when the package is verified and public-safe.

entries.plain_meaning: A selected-128 baseline using metadata or text-derived public-safe features.
entries.project_usage: Compares simple and neural heads on the held-out split.
entries.do_not_confuse_with: Raw video, depth, or audio feature baselines.

entries.plain_meaning: A simple non-neural task head; the "minimum" reference row in casual wording.
entries.project_usage: Provides a reproducible lower-complexity comparison for task feasibility.

entries.plain_meaning: A compact neural task head.
entries.project_usage: Used for single-episode and selected-128 baseline comparisons.

entries.plain_meaning: The Qwen3-Omni run lineage.
entries.project_usage: v1-v4 are earlier pipeline/ablation evidence, v5 is the prior pinned release, and v6 is the current public 20-task row.

entries.plain_meaning: The multimodal foundation-model family used for the Qwen branch.
entries.project_usage: The current public 20-task Qwen row is Qwen3-Omni v6 LoRA plus task-specific probes.

entries.plain_meaning: A selected-128 baseline using exported public-safe raw-feature groups.
entries.project_usage: Tracks what non-foundation heads can do with richer processed inputs.

entries.plain_meaning: A non-neural baseline family for the selected-128 rows.
entries.project_usage: Used for metadata/text and raw-feature 128-episode comparisons before NN/foundation-model rows.

entries.plain_meaning: Learning geometry and spatial reasoning from egocentric data.
entries.project_usage: Uses video, depth, camera pose, and language tasks to target 3D/space reasoning.

entries.plain_meaning: Mapping perception and language to action chunks.
entries.project_usage: A future policy/VLA direction that needs action-target conversion and stronger policy packaging.

entries.plain_meaning: Hugging Face dataset repo for derived evidence.
entries.project_usage: Stores public-safe reports, metrics, website JSON, and sanitized result packages.

entries.plain_meaning: Hugging Face model repo for lightweight baseline artifacts.
entries.project_usage: Mirrors baseline weights, figures, metrics, and task artifacts.

entries.plain_meaning: Hugging Face-hosted app/site surface.
entries.project_usage: Mirrors the dashboard and static website assets.
entries.do_not_confuse_with: HF artifact dataset or model repo.

entries.plain_meaning: A consolidated public-safe model-result bundle.
entries.project_usage: Groups baseline weights, verified model artifacts, analysis files, and manifests.

entries.plain_meaning: A check that public copies match the source files.
entries.project_usage: Records whether GitHub, website, and HF mirrors agree.

entries.plain_meaning: A file that can be mirrored publicly without raw gated content.
entries.project_usage: Metrics, JSON summaries, model cards, figures, derived manifests, and approved lightweight weights/adapters.

entries.plain_meaning: A public-package validation report.
entries.project_usage: Confirms required files exist and forbidden raw/private assets are not included.

entries.plain_meaning: A result or artifact bundle that passed local/public validators.
entries.project_usage: Only verified packages are promoted to README, website, and HF surfaces as public evidence.
